stops.note: meant "to sweet-talk, to flirt," related to ghazaal, "young gazelle"
developed into a lyric poetic form of rhyming couplets on love and loss
flourished further as a major poetic form in Mughal India
entered English literary criticism and was later adopted by English-language poets

current_meaning: a lyric poem made of rhyming couplets, traditionally on themes of love and loss, originating in Arabic and developed in Persian and Urdu literature
